title: Truly Fabulous
body:
The application packs many many features in a simple bucket and super effective in terms of motivation. Referring to Fabulous as an “app” would be an understatement, since it’s kind of a one stop shop for a healthy, happy mindset.

Within 10 days (that’s the duration I’ve signed up for premium) I certainly feel more energetic, less resistive, more acceptive and positive in just a short time. The key point to let this app have a positive effect in your life is to be ready to accept this change initially without a prejudice and say “I’m ready!” Then app will handle the rest.

“So, if everything so fabulous, why 3 stars?” Because in the last 7 days, I’m asked for a rating on AppStore repetitively, sharing a 30-day premium guest pass at least 3 times, and finally today an offer to upgrade to a life time plan for a 10-times the price of annual subscription. Needless to say, I’ve already signed up for an annual subscription. This is not good Fabulous. You’re suggesting and motivating to have healthy financial decisions, eliminate distractors from our daily life for a more focused an healthy mindset. When I launch the app at 08:00am in the morning, I don’t want to be interrupted with a “Would you like to review us on AppStore?” Question. That’s not what I signed up for. You need to understand that your users could be in a very fragile state, that cannot even handle these kind of frequent “enforcements”. I don’t mean to exaggerate and offend anyone, but nobody with a clear, healthy mindset would need an application like this. I can expect this kind of distractors from Facebook, but not from you. Let’s roll for a few months, then you ask for endorsements. How can you even be sure that the journey will be successful? Of course every company needs financial power to thrive and achieve more, but these annoyances contradict with your prime mission.

title: Highly recommended
body:
I am so happy to have found this app; its graphics are attractive, the written letters are very assuring and the experience as a whole is very supportive. 
The app can be used free of charge, if you want to try its other features out, you can subscribe to the Sphere. 

One thing I did not enjoy was the insistent subscription messages I received during my first habit. I think they should be brought to the user’s attention after 2 weeks of use, or following two completed habits. I nearly gave up using the app because of this insistent behaviour.

Right now, I am happy to be using the app and I have a monthly subscription. I will consider upgrading provided that I am still using the app at the end of the month.
